The School Garden Project: 班级把荒地改造成菜园的项目。
Last term, our class had an interesting idea: the empty land behind the school could become a vegetable garden. Our teacher, Ms Brown, loved the plan and asked the head teacher for permission.

In March, we started the work. Some students dug the hard soil, while others collected old bottles and stones. A student's father brought young plants and seeds from his farm. We planted tomatoes, carrots and beans in small groups, and each group had its own corner.

The hardest part was the summer holiday. Nobody was at school, so the plants almost died. Luckily, the school keeper, Mr Hill, watered them twice a week. When we came back in September, the garden was full of life.

In October, we picked the vegetables and made a big salad together. We also sold some carrots to parents and gave the money to a local animal home. The garden project taught us that patience and teamwork can turn empty land into something wonderful.
